newsitem.title: GERMANY: Strong reserves help German call money rates ease.
newsitem.headline: Strong reserves help German call money rates ease.

text.p: German call money was trading at around the Bundesbank's three percent securities repurchase rate on Friday in a quiet market, and traders said market rates could even slip below that level in late trade.
Earlier call money was quoted in a narrow range of 3.00/02 compared with 3.00/05 late on Thursday. But rates slipped to straddle the three percent level in early afternoon trade.

Traders said good reserve data were pushing rates lower. Minimum reserves held at the central bank totalled 38.4 billion marks on Thursday, down from 39,6 billion on Wednesday. But the average for the month was an unchanged 39.4 billion.
Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average FIONA= stood at 3.03933 percent on Friday, after 3.04000on Thursday.
